claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, John D. Rateliff (ed.), "Addendum: The Seventh Phase: iv. Personae", The History of The Hobbit, 2011 p. 900

claims.text: While Bifur was descended from the Dwarves of Moria, he himself was not of Durin's line. He was a cousin of the brothers Bofur and Bombur.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "Durin's Folk"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "Inside Information"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "Flies and Spiders"

claims.text: Bifur was older than Fíli and Kíli (b. ) at least "by some fifty years", but younger than Balin (b. ), since it was said that Balin was "the eldest left" after Thorin's capture.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "Durin's Folk"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "Over Hill and Under Hill"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "Barrels Out of Bond"

claims.text: By Bifur was living in Erebor, as Glóin told Frodo Baggins at Rivendell.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Fellowship of the Ring, "Many Meetings"

claims.text: In the wolves' glade Bifur shared a pine tree with Bofur, Bombur, and Thorin.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "Out of the Frying-Pan into the Fire"
claims.section: section == History == > The Quest of Erebor

claims.text: When Gandalf was telling the story of the company's adventures to Beorn, Bifur, Bofur, and Bombur were the last of the Dwarves to show up.
claims.section: section == History == > The Quest of Erebor

claims.text: After the barrel ride down the River Running both Bifur and Bofur came out fairly dry and not very knocked about, but they lay down and refused to do anything.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "A Warm Welcome"
claims.section: section == History == > The Quest of Erebor

claims.text: On the doorstep on the side of the Lonely Mountain, when Thorin commented that the next day was the beginning of the last week of autumn, Bifur pointedly added, "And winter comes after autumn".
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "On the Doorstep"
claims.section: section == History == > The Quest of Erebor

claims.text: Bifur fought in and survived the Battle of Five Armies. He was given his share of the treasure by Dáin Ironfoot, and made his home in Erebor.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "The Return Journey"
claims.section: section == History == > The Quest of Erebor

claims.text:
In one of the earliest manuscript fragments of The Hobbit, Bifur and Bofur went into the hall and came back with their walking sticks, which they turned into clarinets. In the published text the two Dwarves came back from the hall with clarinets that they had left with their walking sticks. John Rateliff (author of The History of The Hobbit) said that in the earliest phase Tolkien had added fairy tale touches of Dwarven magic to emphasize the uncanny, other-worldly nature of the Dwarves as opposed to Bilbo.
Originally, when Bombur needed propping up in Mirkwood after being cut from the spiders' webbing, it was his cousins Bifur and Bofur who provided support. In the published story this was changed to Bombur's cousin Bifur and brother Bofur. Also, in the earlier version, when Smaug first came out and the Dwarves in the valley had to be hauled up to the Back Door, Bifur cried out to save Bombur and Bofur, who were both his brothers. In the published text Bifur cried out for his two cousins.
In Tolkien's unfinished 1960 rewrite of The Hobbit, Bifur, Bofur and Bombur were Thorin's attendants. John D. Rateliff assumes this made them either courtiers or honor-guard.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, John D. Rateliff (ed.), "The First Phase: The Bladorthin Typescript", The History of The Hobbit: Mr. Baggins, 2007, p. 36; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "An Unexpected Party"; J.R.R. Tolkien, John D. Rateliff (ed.), "The Second Phase: Mirkwood", The History of The Hobbit: Mr. Baggins, 2007, p. 313; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "Flies and Spiders"; J.R.R. Tolkien, John D. Rateliff (ed.), "The Second Phase: Conversations with Smaug", The History of The Hobbit: Mr. Baggins, 2007; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Hobbit, "Inside Information"; J.R.R. Tolkien, John D.
